chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf narrated to us from Amr ibn Jami' from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:

Whoever finds pleasure in meeting God, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection with the testimony that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God in his record, and the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and it will be said to him: 'O friend of God, enter from whichever of them you wish,' then let him say when morning comes:

'Praise be to God who took away the night by His power and brought the day by His mercy as a new creation. Welcome to the guardians, and may God greet the two scribes.' Then he turns to his right, then to his left, and says: 'Write:

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, I bear witness that there is no god but God, alone without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. And I bear witness that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, and that God will resurrect those in the graves. Upon that I live, and upon that I die, and upon that I will be raised, God willing. O God, convey my greetings of peace to Muhammad and his family.'

key_terms.أبواب الجنة الثمانية: The eight gates of Paradise, each for a specific type of worship
key_terms.الحافظين: The guardian angels who watch over a person
key_terms.صحيفة: Scroll or record of deeds, maintained by recording angels for each person
key_terms.كاتبين: The two scribes/recording angels who record one's deeds

ai.seo_question: What is the morning supplication taught by the Prophet Muhammad for entering Paradise through any of its eight gates?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) taught a morning supplication that, when recited daily upon waking, would earn the reciter the testimony of faith inscribed in their record of deeds, entry through any of the eight gates of Paradise, and the title of 'friend of God.' This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Sadiq and the chain of Imams, reflects the early Islamic practice of structuring the day with specific remembrances, beginning with praise of God for the transition from night to day, greeting the recording angels, and affirming the core creedal beliefs of Islam.
word_analysis: and may God greet them both
